analysis_results.model_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
analysis_results.training_data: For pre-training, the model uses two unlabeled English corpora: BooksCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015; 800M words) and English Wikipedia (2,500M words). For Wikipedia, only text passages are extracted and lists, tables, and headers are ignored; the paper emphasizes using document-level corpora to preserve long contiguous sequences. The combined pre-training corpus is described as ~3.3B words, and training examples are formed by sampling two spans ("sentences") with total length ≤ 512 WordPiece tokens, with 15% of WordPiece tokens selected for masking.
analysis_results.model_architecture: BERT is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder (Vaswani et al., 2017) using bidirectional self-attention. Two main configurations are reported: BERTBASE with 12 Transformer blocks (L=12), hidden size 768 (H=768), 12 attention heads (A=12), and ~110M parameters; and BERTLARGE with 24 blocks (L=24), hidden size 1024, 16 heads, and ~340M parameters (feed-forward size is 4H). Inputs use a 30k WordPiece vocabulary with summed token, segment (sentence A/B), and position embeddings, plus special tokens [CLS] and [SEP]; pre-training uses masked language modeling (MLM) and next sentence prediction (NSP).
analysis_results.limitations: The paper notes a key pre-train/fine-tune mismatch: the [MASK] token used in MLM does not appear during fine-tuning, which they mitigate via an 80/10/10 masking strategy (mask/random/unchanged). It also states that fine-tuning BERTLARGE can be unstable on small datasets, requiring multiple random restarts to obtain good results. Additionally, longer sequences are disproportionately expensive because self-attention cost is quadratic in sequence length, motivating a training schedule that uses length 128 for 90% of steps and length 512 for the remaining 10%.
